🎲 Rarity Chances

Adjust the weight of each rarity with the slider or by typing an exact number. Weights do not need to sum to 100 — the percentage under each slider shows that rarity's actual chance of being rolled, based on its share of the total weight below. These weights are also used to roll rarity for the Store's daily items. Every batch of Random loot also has a small chance of including a monster part sourced from a real creature matching the best rarity rolled — same odds as everywhere else parts drop, adjustable from the Combat tab's "Monster Loot Settings" panel.

⚖ Modifier Weights

These sliders control how likely each type of modifier is to appear on a generated unique item. Higher weight = appears more often. Weights are relative — they don't need to sum to 100. Spells & Buffs are weighted heavier by default to reward spellcasters and create more interesting items. Changes apply immediately to new items generated above, and to the Store's daily items.

⚡ Power / Spell

Grants ability to cast a spell at a certain frequency. Scales with rarity.

8

⬆ Buff (Self / Ally)

Grants a stat bonus or advantage to the bearer, or lets the bearer grant one to an ally. Number of allied targets scales with rarity.

7

⬇ Debuff (Enemy / Curse)

Usually inflicts a penalty or condition on an enemy; occasionally a curse the bearer suffers instead. Severity scales with rarity.

5

🎭 Named Trait

A fixed personality (e.g. "Bloody": +Strength, -Constitution) — always the same buff/debuff pair. Both amounts scale with rarity, and the buff is always the larger of the two.

4

🌀 Transform

Allows bearer to transform into a creature. Duration and form scale with rarity.

3

👁 Summon

Summons an entity to serve. Power and duration scale dramatically with rarity.

3

🗺 Terrain

Alters the physical environment. Radius and permanence scale with rarity.

2

🗡 Skill

Grants mastery of a combat or utility skill with a proficiency bonus.

4

🐉 Monster Skill

Grants one random attack drawn from a random creature in the Monster Compendium, tiered by rarity.

4

⚗ Tag Compatibility System

The generator uses a tag system to prevent nonsensical modifier combinations and promote thematic coherence. Each base item is automatically assigned tags based on its name (fire, cold, storm, shadow, holy, arcane, nature, void, melee, ranged). Modifiers are then drawn from a synergy-weighted pool — modifiers that share a tag with the base item get a bonus weight multiplier, while conflicting tags get suppressed.

Fire items → fire/burn/radiant buffs boosted, cold/storm suppressed
Cold items → cold/frost/storm buffs boosted, fire suppressed
Shadow items → necrotic/stealth/void boosted, holy suppressed
Holy items → radiant/healing/divine boosted, shadow/void suppressed
Arcane items → spell power/teleport/force boosted broadly
Nature items → beast/druid/terrain/healing boosted

Generated item cards show their detected tags and a synergy note explaining what the tag system did for that item.

🩸 The Fleshmancer

A cellar that smells of formaldehyde and copper. Jars line every shelf, and something in them is always still twitching.

Summon three freshly harvested limbs. Each one rolls its own effects first — the limb's rarity is determined by how strong those effects turn out, not chosen ahead of time. Pick one, pay to have it grafted on, and see whether the flesh takes. A successful graft is added straight to your item list, ready to equip from the Inventory tab.

🩸 Rework Crafting Material

Or drag a monster part in here instead — no gamble, no chance of rejection. It's reworked straight into a graft ready to attach. The better the part's own rarity, the stronger (and, at the highest tiers, the more numerous) its beneficial effects will be.

🎯 Bounty Hunter

A corkboard thick with wanted posters, each one promising coin for blood — or capture, if you're feeling generous.

Three bounties are posted at a time, each a different rarity, each pulled fresh from the full creature registry — don't be surprised if one of them turns out to be a person. Every bounty's target, and any escort guards it has, are rolled as real creatures the moment the bounty is posted (hobgoblin soldiers really do roll as Hobgoblins; something more exotic falls back to a similar low-tier creature of the target's own kind). Hit Save on whichever bounties you actually want to use — that registers them under their own names, searchable from the Combat tab's creature search to add to a fight, so the registry only fills up with the ones you chose to keep. Claim a bounty for its reward whenever you're done with it.

🔧 The Monster Mangler

A workbench cluttered with vices, tongs, and the smell of scorched hide. He'll work anything into anything — for a price.

Drag a monster part into the first slot and a weapon or piece of armor into the second — he'll reforge them into a brand-new item with an effect themed to that part and scaled by its rarity, for a fee based on both their rarities. Click a slot below to filter "Your Items" down to only what fits there. Both the part and the original item are consumed — the reforged result lands in Finished Work below, where you can save it to your Token Library or discard it before mangling again.

Armor Class, saving throws, and skills are computed automatically from your ability scores and equipped gear — hover a green/red value to see which item is affecting it. Item bonuses are picked up by scanning each item's effect text for patterns like "+2 Strength" or "+1 AC" — a best-effort match, not a guaranteed-complete rules engine.
